Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old woman with 3-week history of left-sided decreased hearing and facial numbness around the left ear/jawline, with intermittent left-sided tinnitus and occasional dizziness; clinician suspects possible Bell’s palsy; plan for same-day in-person GP assessment for neurological and ear examination.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left-sided hearing difficulty and left facial numbness.
- Onset/duration: ~3 weeks.
- Course: Persistent numbness “quite often/all the time”; hearing decreased on the left; intermittent ringing in the left ear; occasional dizziness associated with ringing.
- Location: Left side—around the left ear and along the jawline.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent tinnitus (left), occasional dizziness.
- Pertinent negatives: No ear discharge, no ear pain, no fever, no ear itch noted; no weakness or numbness in limbs; no difficulty swallowing or speaking; no visual problems.
- Impact: Reduced training at work (jockey) due to symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps (intermittent symptoms).
- Remote history of “labyrinthitis” (patient-reported; no ongoing issues).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
- Nasal spray for nasal polyps (name and dose/route/frequency not documented; prescribed previously).
- OTC Rennie’s as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
Allergies:
- Latex.
- No known drug allergies (per patient).

Social History:
- Occupation: Jockey; training reduced due to symptoms.
- Living situation: Initially stated living alone, then stated living with partner (conflict noted).
- Pets: None.
- Tobacco, alcohol, substances: Not documented.

Family History:
- Brother with neurofibromatosis (type not specified).
- Otherwise non-contributory per patient.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person examination performed (video visit).
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- No documented exam findings.

Investigations:
- None performed/reported during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left-sided decreased hearing with left facial numbness (3 weeks), intermittent tinnitus, occasional dizziness.
  - Assessment: Clinician suspects possible Bell’s palsy (preliminary impression); needs confirmation with physical exam and neurological assessment; otoscopic exam to evaluate ear pathology.
  - Plan:
    - Same-day, face-to-face GP assessment today.
    - Neurological examination including cranial nerves.
    - Otoscopic ear examination.
    - Clinician to message admin to arrange; patient to call support team in ~5 minutes to secure a convenient Central London clinic slot today.
    - Reassured patient that, based on history, this does not appear life-threatening; definitive reassurance pending physical examination.
- Issue 2: Intermittent tinnitus with occasional dizziness.
  - Assessment: Associated with primary complaint; etiology to be evaluated.
  - Plan:
    - Assess during same-day in-person visit; include ear examination and neurological assessment.
- Issue 3: Work impact (reduced training as a jockey).
  - Assessment: Symptoms affecting occupational function.
  - Plan:
    - To be addressed following in-person assessment (no specific plan documented today).

General Plan:
- Ensure the appointment is completed today as instructed.
- Further explanation of Bell’s palsy and management to be provided if diagnosis confirmed after examination.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; complete physical exam; complete medication list with names/doses/frequency; detailed ROS; smoking/alcohol/substance history; immunizations; problem list; baseline hearing status.
- Internal conflicts: Living situation—patient stated living alone, then living with partner (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some brief pauses/ellipses but no major inaudible sections.
